SELECT COUNT(1) AS n
FROM   TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss
LEFT JOIN TPCDS_DB.promotion p ON ss.ss_item_sk = p.p_item_sk
WHERE  ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query scans the large store_sales table with a filter on ss_customer_sk IS NULL, then performs a broadcast left outer join to promotion where the right key p_item_sk is not unique (293 rows, 291 distinct), causing row multiplication that inflates the input to the final aggregation.

plan_nodes.note: LeftOuter BuildRight; Left keys [1]: [ss_item_sk#39532]; Right keys [1]: [p_item_sk#39557]; Join type: LeftOuter; Join c

hypotheses.claim: A LEFT JOIN whose columns are never read still costs a join; if the joined key is unique it cannot change the rows and can be removed. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on ss.ss_item_sk = p.p_item_sk)
The BroadcastHashJoin produces many more rows than the filtered store_sales input because promotion.p_item_sk has duplicate values, increasing the work for downstream aggregation.
The parquet scan of store_sales with pushed IsNull filter reads a large portion of the table; if the null fraction of ss_customer_sk is high, this scan dominates elapsed time.

The partial HashAggregate processes the multiplied row stream from the join; reducing the row count (e.g., by deduplicating the right side or eliminating the join if semantically valid) would shrink aggregation input.
